question.leadin: Give the following about military surprise attacks launched during holidays.
question.text: During this war, communist forces launched the 1968 Tet Offensive during a Lunar New Year ceasefire. The coordinated effort attacked numerous cities, include Hue and Saigon.
question.clue: Outrage also came out of the massacre of villagers by William Cailey in My Lai.

swap.text: The volcanoes Mount Pinatubo (pin-uh-TOO-boh) and Mount Mayon (mah-YAWN) are located on this island, the largest in the Philippines.
swap.clue: This island, which sits to the south of the Babuyan Islands, is also home to the basin of the Cagayan River and Clark Air Base, which was heavily damaged by another of its volcanoes.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Asian political families.
question.text: One member of this family dealt with the aftermath of Typhoon Haiyan in 2013. His mother Corazon's controversial 1986 election loss led to the People Power Revolution.
question.clue: A member of this family, who was supported by Cardinal Sin, founded the Lakas ng Bayan Party and was assassinated at an airport which now bears his name.

swap.leadin: This man fought his emotions while announcing the failure of a national merger.
swap.text: Name this founding father of an Asian city-state that became independent from Malaysia in 1965. This leader passed away in March 2015.
swap.clue: This man's government created the Social Development Unit, a state-backed matchmaking agency designed to reverse the effects of his overly-successful "Stop at Two" population control policy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Chinese diaspora in Southeast Asia.
question.text: Chinese mining companies known as kongsi operated in this modern-day country before their suppression by the Dutch East Indies. This country is governed from Jakarta.
question.clue: The resort island of Bali is part of this country, which was devastated by a 2004 tsunami and the eruption of Krakatoa in 1883.

swap.text: This famous duo from early Vietnamese history led a rebellion against the Chinese Han Dynasty before being defeated and committing suicide by drowning.
swap.clue: The movement led by this group collapsed after they ordered a retreat behind the Jin River, after which this group drowned themselves in the Hat river.

question.leadin: In this country, the Briggs Plan resettled the rural population into "new villages" to combat Chin Peng's MNLA guerillas.
question.text: Name this country where the British fought a 12-year insurgency called the Emergency. In 1965, a city-state led by Lee Kuan Yu separated from this country, whose states include Johor and Malacca.
question.clue: This country has a rotating constitutional kingship known as the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

swap.text: This Filipino revolutionary led rebel forces during the Philippine-American War. He later served as the first president of the Philippines.
swap.clue: Earlier, he quarreled with Andres Bonifacio over divisions in the Katipunan movement.

question.leadin: A group of communist rebels in this country formed the Hukbalahap during World War II.
question.text: Name this modern-day country where the Sakdal Uprising and the Moro Crater Massacre took place.
question.clue: In this country, after the surrender of the fortress of Corregidor, thousands of troops went on a "death march" through Baatan.

swap.leadin: A man named Mongkut spent 25 years as a monk before becoming the king of this country in 1851.
swap.text: Name this country that has been ruled by several kings named Rama from the Chakri Dynasty since the 18th century.
swap.clue: Since 1957, this country has criminalized insults against its monarchy under its lese-majeste laws.

question.text: 1. points) These twin towers in Kuala Lumpur took over the title of world's tallest building from the Sears Tower on their completion in 1996.

swap.leadin: In this modern-day country, the badass Naresuan [nah-ray-SOO-un] was a leader of the Ayutthaya [ah-YOO-tee-ah] Kingdom.
swap.text: Name this Southeast Asian country that was ruled by war criminal and former Manchester City owner Thaksin Shinawatra.
swap.clue: Its rulers used the Paknam Incident to create an irredentist nationalism later deployed by the Phibun government.

question.text: During the Lam Son uprising, this Vietnamese leader successfully rebelled against the Ming dynasty. This leader legendarily possessed the sword "Heaven's Will," allowing him to change his height at will.
question.clue: This ruler developed a namesake law code based on that of the Tang, and he introduced the quan đien ("kwan dyen") system of land distribution.

swap.leadin: This empire supplied its cities with water using massive reservoirs called barays ("buh-RYES").
swap.text: Name this empire whose capital city of Angkor used two such barays, whose drying out was a major cause of its collapse.
swap.clue: Among the landmarks in its main capital were the temples Ta Prohm, the Baphuon, and Ta Keo, the first of which was made entirely from sandstone.

question.leadin: This treaty allowed the free importation of opium by British ships into a certain country, mirroring the 'unequal treaties' earlier imposed upon Qing ['ching'] China.
question.text: Name this 1855 treaty negotiated between its namesake, then the Governor of Hong Kong, and a certain Southeast Asian kingdom, which among other things allowed free trade by foreigners in Bangkok.

swap.leadin: A king of this dynasty founded an order of Buddhism called Dhammayut and served as the first abbot of the Wat Bowonniwet Vihara.
swap.text: Name this dynasty whose viceroy Pinklao was the younger brother of King Mongkut, who negotiated the Bowring Treaty liberalizing foreign trade.
swap.clue: This dynasty's first ruler solidified power by winning the Nine Armies War, and it allowed free trade within its territory by agreeing to the Bowring Treaty, which replaced the Burney Treaty.

question.leadin: This dictator, who bathed in dolphin blood to stay young, betrayed his ancestry by persecuting ethnic Chinese with the Enterprise Nationalization Law of 1963.
question.text: Name this autocratic Prime Minister who ruled for 26 years after using the Union Revolutionary Council to seize power in 1962, after which he released an ideological tract titled as his country's "way to socialism."
question.answerHtml: <u>Ne Win</u> [or U <u>Ne Win</u>; accept Thakin <u>Shu Maung</u>; prompt on “<u>Ne</u>” or “<u>Win</u>” or “<u>Shu</u>” or “<u>Maung</u>”]
question.clue: Nu was deposed by this general, who infamously replaced Burma's 50- and 100-kyat bills with 45- and 90-kyat bills just because they were divisible by the lucky number nine. The 8888 Uprising toppled this socialist dictator, who notably bathed in dolphins' blood to stay young.

swap.leadin: A gluttonous ruler of this kingdom sometimes displayed good judgment, like when he bragged about swallowing 300 dishes of curry daily, and sometimes displayed bad judgment, like when he provoked a Mongol invasion.
swap.text: Name this first kingdom to unify Burma, which was ruled by Narathihapate (nuh-rah-thee-hah-puh-tay) and was expanded to much of the Irrawaddy valley by Anawrahta (uh-naw-ruh-tah).
swap.answerHtml: Pagan (puh-gaan) Kingdom [or Pagan Empire; or Bagan Kingdom; or Bagan Empire]
swap.clue: After King Manuha refused to give him a copy of the Triptaka, a king of this empire captured Manuha and 30,000 residents of the Thaton Kingdom in order to relocate them to his capital.

question.text: Mandatory collective farming was abandoned in 1988 as part of the Đoi Moi reforms, which were implemented after the death of this successor to Ho Chi Minh as General Secretary.
question.clue: This successor of Ho Chi Minh as Vietnam's general secretary, who oversaw the Cambodian-Vietnamese and Sino-Vietnamese wars. He shared his surname with a dynasty that nominally ruled Đai Viet from 1427 to 1789 despite Mac opposition.

swap.text: This Indonesian diplomat organized the Bandung Convention, and later served as ambassador to the United Nations under Suharto.
